native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: In the 18th century BCE (1800-1701 BCE) — the first century in the 4100-500 BCE record where the two cultural-capital diversity indicators diverge — Diversity in Pottery Decoration increased significantly (Zkeverz -0.48 -> +0.97, Δ=+1.45 z-scores) while Diversity in Pottery Form declined simultaneously (ZKeform +0.74 -> -1.13, Δ=-1.87 z-scores, a record low). This is the earliest chronological opposite-trend event; before it the two series co-move. Robust across a threshold sweep (θ=0, 0.5, 1.0, and 90th-percentile ≈0.555) and identical for raw, interpolated, and capital.csv values. Alternative label under an end-point convention: 17th century BCE (1700-1601 BCE).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded all 3 CSVs with correct decimal handling (time_series_data.csv = period; capital.csv and pollen = comma/EU). 2) Verified CE = 1950 - calBP exactly (max abs diff 0.0); cultural record 4100-500 BCE, raw cultural-capital Z-values present only at 37 centennial points. 3) Confirmed raw centennial values == _inter at anchors == capital.csv ZKeform/Zkeverz (max abs diff 0.0000). 4) Derived centuries from CE (oldest->newest) and computed the century-to-century simple difference d (== 100-yr slope) for PotteryDecoration and PotteryForm; used simple difference not % change because values are signed z-scores. 5) Applied (Deco d>0 AND Form d<0, with magnitude threshold) and swept θ = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 90th-pct(≈0.555); earliest qualifying century identical in all cases = 18th c. BCE. 6) Labeled per standard convention (18th c. BCE = 1800-1701 BCE), noting the 17th-c. BCE alternative. 7) Cross-referenced culture phases (LN->OBA) and pollen openness as context only.
